notes: Unit of labelling is a GEO series. "screen" = the series itself holds pooled guide-count reads (mixed series count). SuperSeries and the RNA-seq/ChIP/ATAC SubSeries of screen papers are not_screen. single_cell = CRISPR screen with single-cell readout.
Inputs are GDS esummary records only (title, summary, sample titles, organism); SRA library strategy was not used in this evaluation although discover() can add it.

Source sets: orcs_linked = every GEO series elinked from the PMIDs of BioGRID ORCS screens (includes many non-screen SubSeries of screen papers: realistic hard negatives); discovery_2025-03 = every GSE the GEO discovery query returned for 2025-03-01..20; targeted_title_* = GSEs with screen words in the title (biased toward easy positives; used only to reach 100+ positives).
Split is a deterministic sha256 hash of the accession (30% test). Rules and weights were changed only while looking at train-split rows; the test split was scored once after tuning stopped.
Labels were made by one annotator (the agent) from GEO title/summary/sample names; label_confidence low/medium marks judgement calls.

Rescored once after a spec-compliance change (not a test-driven one): a CRISPR study with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq / CROP-seq) is now always "maybe", whatever its score. Before the change, test split: screen P 0.885 R 0.605 F1 0.719; screen|maybe P 0.72 R 0.923 F1 0.809.

Rescored a second time after adding the "unsupported organism named in the text" rule (for records with no taxonomy). The rule was written for bacterial CRISPRi studies seen in live ENA discovery, but it also fixes GSE262333 (Yarrowia, organism filed as synthetic construct), a test-split error already seen. So test precision 0.92 is NOT a clean held-out number; the last clean test figures are screen P 0.885 R 0.605 F1 0.719, screen|maybe P 0.72 R 0.923 F1 0.809.
